records.reason: m117 at 20/1, 150 ul, and a 600 ul DCM plug extends the same-loading donor-containing aldehyde curve beyond measured lower ratios. Its wide V1 model range makes it useful for separating a ratio threshold from smooth onset movement; measured m117 rows e55c8ef232b46d3a1ca9 and 1d15ee46756cd1845a68 show condition-sensitive behavior.

m211 at 50/1 and only 50 ul directly tests the strong-ratio, low-loading corner after the measured 10/1 and 50/1 rows dd4829f39cdf781ffaf9 and 0f06772820e6693753e3. The large V1 width targets the unresolved basic heteroaromatic transition.

m216 at 1/1 PE and 50 ul supplies a low-strength point between the measured early PE behavior ae187d6f3746213b630c and the delayed 5/1 to 10/1 PE rows. It can locate the onset of the sharp nitrogen-associated condition transition.

m141 at 10/1 DCM and 50 ul is a matched loading contrast to the measured 10/1, 150 ul row 6f548d72f01fc85debdc and the 5/1, 50 ul row 434ffacb33eccce497c5. It tests whether loading mainly changes V1, V2, or both in a basic heteroaromatic scaffold.

m146 at 10/1, 150 ul, DCM fills a high-width loading point beside the measured high-retention m146 rows 9e3ce3497298084abd83 and 51f5ae6a991eea9e720e. This distinguishes a scaffold-specific tail from a transferable nitrogen correction.

m90 at 2/1 and 150 ul connects measured 2/1 and stronger-ratio m90 behavior, including 0460dfc4e1747f0fc92c and 96710afeabc594baa359. It is a useful interpolation point for separate V1 and V2 response curves.

m161 at 2/1 and 100 ul is a loading midpoint between measured 2/1 rows e12edd0198c0d750ecd5 and 0ced19fd8372ed93361c. The wide V1 interval tests whether the amino nitrile response changes smoothly with volume.

m160 at 0/1 and 50 ul supplies the weak-solvent, low-loading anchor missing around the measured amino nitrile series. It helps prevent the high-ratio m160 tail from being extrapolated into the early regime.

m159 at 5/1 and 150 ul probes the boundary between the measured compact low-ratio rows and the severe high-ratio responses a17bcdddcf0799baeee2 and 1395836aef00d6a880b0. It tests whether the tail is ratio-triggered, loading-triggered, or jointly controlled.

m82 at 10/1, 150 ul, with a 200 ul DCM plug extends the measured 10/1 low-volume point 3c041f5186a291c3b313. The broad V1 range is valuable for learning the loading dependence of a strongly tail-prone acceptor-rich family.

m168 at 20/1 and 150 ul is a high-width condition-response point for a flexible diketone family. It provides coverage in a region where carbonyl count and polarity alone have not reliably predicted endpoint tails.
m168 at 50/1 and 100 ul complements the selected 20/1 point with a stronger ratio and lower loading. The pair discriminates a smooth solvent response from a localized completion threshold.

m197 at 50/1 PE and 100 ul targets a high-width phenolic aldehyde condition. It extends donor-containing aromatic coverage into a strong-solvent regime where V2 tails can be scaffold-specific rather than proportional to V1.

m193 at 20/1, 150 ul, and a 700 ul DCM plug tests the loading response of a nitrobenzaldehyde family already showing delayed high-ratio behavior, including measured rows a5f9179bfb146ad70953 and a01a137fa48c1391b9e7. The large endpoint width is useful for V2 calibration.

m125 at 5/1 and 100 ul fills the loading midpoint between the measured 50 ul and 150 ul high-ratio rows 761c3f82d640da44966c and 06ebbf6e52fa3ea6aef3. It tests whether the completion tail changes continuously with sample volume.

m125 at 2/1 and 50 ul probes the low-loading side of the striking measured 2/1 response 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4 and the selected 2/1, 150 ul point 19f19f196ba5787a01b0. This is a high-information local threshold experiment.

m125 at 2/1 and 150 ul with a 500 ul DCM plug is a matched amount point against measured 19f19f196ba5787a01b0, while changing the loading-solvent volume. It can reveal whether the apparent V2 anomaly is tied to the plug condition as well as the mobile phase.

m125 at 1/1 and 50 ul supplies an early, low-loading anchor for the same scaffold. Together with the selected 2/1 and 5/1 points, it constrains whether the response surface has a sharp onset or a broad tail.

m99 at 0/1 and a 1000 ul DCM plug probes loading-solvent-volume effects in a donor-containing ester. It complements the measured high-loading m99 behavior d8fcb58722028dbf9c02 and can separate plug effects from general amount effects.

m207 at 2/1 and 100 ul bridges measured low-ratio low-loading behavior and the delayed 5/1 and 10/1 alcohol rows 4e5ead91320bd24d485e and ff3b6b1069b7d66ad021. It tests attachment-position and loading effects within the donor family.

m28 at 10/1 and 100 ul targets a high-width carbonyl point between measured low-ratio rows 686562279e2bfb73ef1e and 08d345874afeaea97b5e and the stronger high-loading regime. It teaches whether onset and completion cross a condition threshold independently.

m40 at 50/1 and 50 ul is a high-strength, low-loading carbonyl control adjacent to the measured 50/1, 100 ul row c2334ccf8e6788ac6ca2. The contrast tests amount sensitivity in a family with substantial V2 spread.

m75 at 20/1 PE and 100 ul samples an intermediate solvent ratio and loading between measured lower-ratio rows and the delayed 50/1 PE outcome 9249ed2c527f70995033. It is useful for learning whether the completion response is gradual or threshold-like.

m45 at 50/1 DCM and 100 ul targets a high-width strong-solvent condition in an ester-bearing scaffold. It broadens coverage of delayed rows while testing whether a large endpoint interval is preserved at lower loading.

m177 at 0/1 and 100 ul with a 1000 ul DCM plug supplies a low-ratio anchor for the nitrobenzophenone series. It can be compared with the measured compact and delayed loading cells 6cf24e264547d6bffd62, 4862e2fb71344ce16021, and b514312eda7950cdcf1c.

m31 at 2/1 and 100 ul tests the onset of a cyano ketone response between measured 2/1 low-loading behavior 2a4de703709973e74dd2 and higher-ratio rows such as b3d9bb5afa82b99f2a11. It helps constrain V1/V2 separately in a lower-complexity acceptor family.

m167 at 0/1 and 50 ul supplies a low-strength fused diketone anchor with a wide predicted V1 interval. It tests whether the broad endpoint behavior seen at stronger ratios is already present at the early boundary.

m40 at 20/1 and 150 ul forms a local ratio/loading contrast with the selected 50/1, 50 ul point. The paired measurements can distinguish solvent-strength effects from amount effects in a fused ketone scaffold.
m184 at 5/1 and 150 ul is a donor-free heavy-halogen calibration anchor at strong solvent. It constrains the model against spreading polar-tail corrections into compact hydrophobic structures.

m174 at 30/1 PE and 150 ul extends the high-width solvent-ratio range for a donor-free aromatic ester. This explores a sparse ratio region while providing a control for whether strong solvent alone generates broad V2 intervals.

m182 at 0/1 and 50 ul supplies the early endpoint of a fused carbonyl response. It complements measured 1/1 through 20/1 behavior, including 52b9af4df1f1e7cd4d9b and 195ef0093f90d8fd51ad, and helps repair onset interpolation.

m199 at 0/1 and 50 ul extends the same-scaffold sulfoxide curve below the measured 1/1, 5/1, and 10/1 cells 741e52b1633ebf2743f3, 714004602e6452764d9a, and aa83ae83c0fa0cc37777. It anchors the onset before the observed completion tail.

hypotheses.content: Basic and heteroaromatic nitrogen families have scaffold- and ratio-dependent retention transitions; nitrogen count and generic polarity descriptors do not determine V1/V2 reliably.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The Row-distribution contains large nitrogen-associated endpoint errors, so matched scaffold and condition cells can teach the model explicit interaction structure instead of applying a global nitrogen offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do nitrogen-associated tails begin at a common solvent threshold, or do scaffold geometry and loading determine separate thresholds?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount, sample volume, loading-solvent volume, and PE/EA ratio interact non-smoothly, with V2 often changing much more than V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local condition-response cells are needed to learn interactions that structure similarity and aggregate loading features cannot infer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: For tail-prone scaffolds, does changing loading primarily delay completion, or can it also move onset across a threshold?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing aromatic structures have geometry- and scaffold-specific adsorption tails; donor count alone is insufficient to predict retention.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs attachment position, fused-ring environment, flexibility, and condition interactions rather than a universal HBD correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor geometries produce long completion tails while retaining early onset, and which remain compact?

hypotheses.content: Large V2 completion tails are concentrated in scaffold, solvent-ratio, and loading neighborhoods rather than being explained by a generic polarity or carbonyl correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-specific local corrections can reduce dominant V2 errors without inflating compact rows across the full distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do intermediate ratio and loading points connect compact and delayed regimes smoothly, or reveal scaffold-specific thresholds?

hypotheses.content: Several simple ketone, ester, fused carbonyl, and nitro families show condition-dependent onset changes that are not proportional to completion changes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Separate V1 and V2 response curves reduce transfer of V2 tail corrections into onset predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which low-complexity carbonyl families show reproducible onset thresholds while completion remains locally calibrated?

hypotheses.content: Compact hydrophobic and weakly interacting heavy-atom rows remain necessary calibration anchors across solvent-ratio and loading changes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls suppress overgeneralization of polar-tail corrections and preserve global V1/V2 calibration in ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do donor-free fused and heavy-halogen structures remain compact at the strongest ratios and altered loadings?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback strengthened the interaction view. m125 showed very different V2 values across nearby 2/1 and 5/1 loading cells, m177 changed from compact to an extreme V2 tail when sample volume increased at 50/1, and m199 developed a large ratio-dependent tail. Nitrogen-associated failures remain substantial for m66, m159, m141, m146, m211, and m216, while fused alcohol rows confirm that donor-containing scaffolds can diverge sharply. Compact heavy-halogen controls remained close enough to support retaining calibration anchors. The next batch therefore emphasizes matched threshold cells and endpoint-specific curves, with controls to keep corrections local.
batch_rationale: The batch repairs the largest observed failure regions while creating several interpretable local response curves. Nitrogen rows cover basic heteroaromatics, amino nitriles, fused nitrogen systems, and loading contrasts. m125, m177, m199, m168, and m82 provide condition-response measurements where V2 tails and loading switches dominate. Donor, nitro, aldehyde, and fused carbonyl rows test whether endpoint corrections transfer across related scaffolds. Heavy-halogen, donor-free, and fused donor-free rows provide compact calibration anchors. This combination should improve generalization by teaching QGeoGNN where interactions and thresholds are needed and where tail corrections must remain suppressed.
